'''''Kleinia neriifolia''''', known in Spanish as ''verode'' or ''berode'', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the daisy family ([[Asteraceae]]).  It is [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] to the [[Canary Islands]]. It was formerly named ''Senecio kleinia''.<ref name=Bramwell>{{cite book|last1=Bramwell|first1=D.|last2=Bramwell|first2=Z.|year=2001|title=Wild flowers of the Canary Islands|publisher=Editorial Rueda|location=Madrid, Spain|isbn=84-7207-129-4}}</ref>{{rp|353}}

==Description==
A [[succulent plant]],<ref name='Oecology'>{{cite book
 | last = Warming
 | first = Eugenius
 | author-link = Eugenius Warming
 | title = Oecology of Plants
 | orig-year = 1909
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=aKXsiOsqlp0C
 | date = 1977
 | publisher = Ayer Publishing
 | location = 300 Bedford Street, Manchester, NH
 | isbn = 0-405-10423-5
 | chapter = 32 Storage of Water by Land Plants
 | chapter-url = https://books.google.com/books?id=aKXsiOsqlp0C&pg=PA123
}}</ref> 
''Kleinia neriifolia'' has articulated branches (constrictions that make them look like rows of sausages)<ref name='cif'>{{cite web
 |url=http://www.canaryislandflora.com/arid.htm 
 |title=Canary Islands Flora - Arid Habitat 
 |access-date=2008-03-02 
 |url-status=dead 
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080306042504/http://www.canaryislandflora.com/arid.htm 
 |archive-date=2008-03-06 
}}</ref>
and thick, stubby, elongated leaves up to {{cvt|12|cm|in|sigfig=1}} long which grow directly from the main stem or branch without a [[petiole (botany)|petiole]] or footstalk. The leaves grow clustered in crowded circles at the tops of the branches.<ref name='cif'/><ref name='Oecology'/> Plants can reach 3 m (10 ft) or more. Fragrant grey white flowers appear at any time between March and October. The plant is [[deciduous]], the leaves falling at the beginning of the dry season.<ref name='digilander'>{{cite web
 | url = https://digilander.libero.it/cacti/PL012.htm
 | title = LE PIANTE - Senecio kleinia
 | access-date = 2008-03-02
 | author = Elio Darcangeli
 | work = PIANTE GRASS and SUCCULANTS
 | language = it
}}</ref>
As with many succulents, reproduction by cuttings is possible.

==Habitat==
{{Quote box
 | quote  = ...these plants almost seem to live on air, yet they attain a considerable size; filled with sap they hang down in all their beauty from jagged rock, at first sight seeming to be purely superficial, but in reality sending their roots into crevices, and abstracting the water retained there by capillarity.
 | source =[[Eugenius Warming]], 1909<ref name='Oecology'/>
 | width  = 33%
 | align  = center
}}
''Kleinia neriifolia'' grows abundantly in the [[Tabaibal-Cardonal]] zone or the arid, subtropical areas, often with steep and eroded [[Substrate (biology)|substrates]] which are more pronounced and dominant in the eastern archipelago.<ref name='Jardín'>{{cite journal
  |author=S. Rivas Goday y F. Esteve Chueca
  | title = Ensayo fitosociológico de la "Crassi-Euphorbieta" macaronesica y estudio de los tabaibales y cardonales de Gran Canaria
  | journal = Anales del Jardín Botánico de Madrid
  | volume =22
  | issue =1
  | pages = 221–339
 | language = es
  | publisher = Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid
  | location = Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid
  | url = http://www.rjb.csic.es/pdfs/Anales_22(1)_221_339.pdf
  | access-date =  2008-03-02}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>  The vegetation can be compared with that of the arid areas of [[Sudan]], [[Ethiopia]], [[Arabia]] and [[Iran]] and is typical of the [[steppe]] in the [[Africa]]n continent.<ref name='cif'/>
{{clr}}

==Horticulture==
The plant is used in gardens with dry conditions.  The plant requires a minimum exposure to the sun.  The minimum winter temperature it can endure is {{convert|-2|°C|°F|sigfig=2}}.<ref name='digilander'/>

''Kleinia neriifolia'' has been successfully cultivated as a houseplant and as landscaping.  It is on a list of suggested fire safe landscaping.<ref name='plumas'>{{cite web
